correctness.rationale: The source proof was reconstructed for every finite nonempty associative idempotent semigroup. For an ideal I, θ(x)=xα(x) sends I into I; θ bijective and I finite gives θ(I)=I. Thus J(θ(x))=J(x). Since xα(x) belongs to the principal ideal of α(x), the J-class poset satisfies J(x)≤J(α(x)), and monotonicity round the finite α orbit yields J(α(x))=J(x). In finite bands J=D, with rectangular classes D=I×Λ and multiplication (i,λ)(j,μ)=(i,μ). Necessarily θ(i,λ)=(i,τ_i(λ)), with τ_i∈S_b, and α(i,λ)=(p_{τ_i(λ)}(i),τ_i(λ)) for p_μ∈S_a. This parametrization is bijective both ways, giving orthomorphism image ∏ S_b on R-classes, (a!)^b constant fibers per D, count ∏(a!)^b(b!)^a and the stated cycle product. Independently enumerated all 41,952 permutations of seven explicitly specified bands, covering rectangular, semilattice-glued, nonuniform-glued and free-left-regular examples; count/image/fiber/cycle values match. The formal proof, not finite enumeration or verifier logs, establishes the universal statement. Identity/singleton class boundaries a=1 or b=1 are correct.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of all complete-mapping orthomorphisms for every finite band, including all Green R-class cycle distributions and constant fiber sizes. These data cannot be inferred solely from existence, and the product formula is invariant under nontrivial changes of cross-D-class multiplication. A researcher studying Cayley-table transversals or finite semigroup cycle behavior could use the precise independent symmetric-group cycle-index formula; it answers a motivated part of a recent cycle-structure question. This is an exact standalone invariant, not a claim to settle arbitrary semigroups or joint α–θ cycles.
